INBOUND (platform adapter): exposes Hermes as an A2A-discoverable agent. An Agent Card is served at /.well-known/agent-card.json (v1.0 canonical path; legacy agent.json also answers) and incoming tasks are routed into the agent's live gateway session like any other platform — so the agent that replies is the same one talking to its user, with full memory and context, not a throwaway clone.
Security is on by default: no bearer token configured => localhost-only bind. Inbound task text passes through prompt-injection filters; outbound text is scrubbed of credential-shaped strings; every exchange is audit-logged and persisted to disk outside the context-compaction pipeline so conversations survive compaction and restarts.

declared_description:
A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol v1.0 support for Hermes Agent — both directions of the open Linux Foundation standard for inter-agent communication.
OUTBOUND (client tools): a2a_discover, a2a_call, a2a_list, a2a_history, and a2a_orchestrate let the agent fetch another agent's Agent Card and send it tasks over JSON-RPC — works with any A2A-compliant peer (Hermes, LangChain, CrewAI, Google ADK, OpenClaw, ...).
INBOUND (platform adapter): exposes Hermes as an A2A-discoverable agent. An Agent Card is served at /.well-known/agent-card.json (v1.0 canonical path; legacy agent.json also answers) and incoming tasks are routed into the agent's live gateway session like any other platform — so the agent that replies is the same one talking to its user, with full memory and context, not a throwaway clone.
Security is on by default: no bearer token configured => localhost-only bind. Inbound task text passes through prompt-injection filters; outbound text is scrubbed of credential-shaped strings; every exchange is audit-logged and persisted to disk outside the context-compaction pipeline so conversations survive compaction and restarts.
Pure stdlib transport (http.server + urllib) — no a2a-sdk dependency required.

The model tool can only make check-ins quieter; more often, resume and wider hours are operator-only via /proactivity or the CLI. After install, the workspace-setup skill walks the agent through setting up Alan's Workspace (a separate desktop app for the user's computer: macOS or Windows) and Tailscale; desktop input goes only through Hermes's approval-gated computer_use tool. Disclosure — once the gateway connects Telegram, a background thread checks every 60 seconds. When the bound Telegram DM has been quiet (2 h by default, doubling per unanswered check-in, 08:00-22:00 user time), it injects an internal user-role prompt into that chat (needs plugins.entries.alans-way.allow_gateway_injection, which setup sets), so the bot runs a turn on its own and may take one \"safe, reversible\" step; the user still approves tool calls in Telegram. Its pre_llm_call/post_llm_call hooks see every session's turns and store the bound chat's activity timestamps in plugin state; optional cross-bot export adds the separate storage disclosed below. On first load it reads $HERMES_HOME/companion/proactivity/proactivity.sqlite3 once, read-only. The plugin itself makes no network calls. The workspace-setup skill has the agent fetch this repo at the catalog pin into ~/alans-way-agents (or reuse a clean clone there) and hand a JSON setup plan to the human in Alan's Workspace. The app runs setup.sh through an external SSH process outside the gateway, checks the exact repoRef and desktopRef and rejects tracked checkout changes; the agent must never run setup or even --verify in its gateway terminal or bypass the lifecycle guard. Windows guests require the human's external Git Bash shell. The human pastes the app's output for review. The external setup does the following. (1) Installs long-running services (Alan's Tools: a managed Chrome/Chromium on a loopback-only debugging port, the first free port from 9223 up, plus a browser broker and an optional availability watcher): systemd units hermes-alans-way-chromium, -browser and mac-watch with loginctl enable-linger where systemd is running; supervisord programs alans-way-chromium, alans-way-browser and alans-way-mac-watch, written to a conf.d file, where it is not (VM images and containers); a KeepAlive LaunchAgent on a macOS guest; logon Scheduled Tasks on Windows. When no X display is running it also installs and runs Xvfb on :99 (unit hermes-alans-way-xvfb or program alans-way-xvfb, -nolisten tcp). (2) Installs packages when they are missing, only as root or with passwordless sudo, through apt, dnf or yum: Google Chrome stable (the current .deb downloaded from dl.google.com on amd64 apt hosts, which also adds Google's apt repository, so the host keeps taking Chrome updates from Google), else the distro chromium package, else Playwright 1.49.1 Chromium through npx (root only); and xvfb. It only warns, and installs nothing, for xdotool, scrot, at-spi2-core and python3-gi, which the VM desktop path needs. (3) Appends the user's computer's public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (administrators_authorized_keys on a Windows admin account) with a from= restriction to the Tailscale ranges 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, rewriting an existing unrestricted line for the same key; pins its host key in known_hosts and adds a ControlMaster block to ~/.ssh/config for Tailscale hosts only (with a tailscale nc ProxyCommand when Tailscale runs in userspace-networking mode). (4) Adds a TimeoutStartSec=180 drop-in to the hermes-gateway unit. Hermes refuses plugin file changes while a gateway is running, so setup drain-stops that profile's gateway (SIGUSR1 under supervisord, else systemctl stop or hermes gateway stop), replays the refused plugin install or update, and starts it again. With --restart it restarts the gateway only if setup changed something the gateway loads (or an earlier restart never happened), detached about ten seconds after printing its summary: by SIGUSR1 drain under supervisord, else a transient systemd-run timer or hermes gateway restart. (5) For the main profile and every profile with its own Telegram bot, writes a managed mcp_servers.workspace_browser block with connect_timeout: 25 seconds (removing other entries that run this router, with a backup; a re-run keeps the computer address and OS it already holds, and --mac-ssh none removes them), turns off the built-in browser toolset for Telegram and cron (--keep-browser only skips disabling it; it does not re-enable a previously disabled toolset), turns computer_use on for Telegram and cron, and sets computer_use.backend to alans-way-computer when it installed or found that provider (under the skill's --skip-plugin flow it only warns and prints the config command). It reads each profile's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN only to derive the numeric bot id. It warns, and changes nothing, when a copy of the workspace-operations skill in a profile's skills directory shadows the plugin's. The workspace router reaches the user's computer over SSH on their tailnet; on the user's computer it calls the local API of Alan's Workspace on 127.0.0.1 with that app's bearer token. The skill's moved-VM checklist has the agent read the app's preferences.json on the user's computer over the same SSH path and tell the human where the VNC password lives without pasting it. The Alan's Workspace setup page has the human run the alans-way connect script from its main branch on their own computer, and the agent may install Tailscale with its official install script. The manual --allow-desktop-actions setup flag, which the skill offers but never adds itself, adds cua:*:background entries to command_allowlist. On a Hermes without the computer-use provider API, including 0.21.5, it also exposes workspace_computer_action, which drives the user's desktop, Terminal included, with no approval. The repo also holds bootstrap-orgo.sh and migrate.sh, which the plugin, setup.sh and the skills never run: a user runs them by hand to provision a fresh supervisord Linux computer (it fetches the Hermes and Tailscale installers over HTTPS, pipes setup.sh from this repo's main branch into bash unless --repo-ref is given, installs openssh-server if absent, writes supervisord programs, and POSTs the Tailscale login URL with a shared secret to a --callback URL when one is given) or to copy ~/.hermes, including .env, auth.json and state.db, to another host over SSH (it also looks up each profile's bot username at api.telegram.org with that profile's bot token). Since 0.21.0, every enabled profile also gets a default-on Telegram texting voice: an additional pre_llm_call hook reads that profile's voice mode and adds a tone note to Telegram turns, and transform_llm_output can remove a known leading assistant opener from the final Telegram reply. Messages containing backticks, quotes, indentation or silence markers are left unchanged by that polish. /tone texting|default|status and hermes tone store the mode under voice in Hermes plugin state; setup.sh --tone applies it to each configured profile. It layers over the user's persona without writing SOUL.md or agent.system_prompt. Check-ins now name one concrete open thread. /proactivity now requests one immediately from the bound chat even when paused or outside active hours, without changing the settings or unanswered-check-in count.
